identity.title: A high-resolution survey of protoplanetary disks in Lupus and the nature of compact disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: Combining archival data and previously published work, we provide a near-complete high resolution image library of 73 protoplanetary (Class II) disks in the Lupus.
Our data were obtained from Cycle 9 observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at Band 6.

evidence.quote: Alternatively, though less likely, we could be observing a different regime where the smallest gaps in our sample are caused by internal photoevaporation rather than planet formation

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Self-calibration was attempted and abandoned for the new datasets

evidence.quote: Self-calibration was attempted on the new datasets, but due to the limited observing time per source and the low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), it was not possible to achieve satisfactory results.

how_they_decided_enough.value: MCMC chains judged converged after discarding 1,000 burn-in steps and inspecting corner plots

evidence.quote: To verify convergence, we discarded the first 1,000 steps (burn-in phase) and examined the corner plots.

limitations_admitted.value: Resolution limits substructure detection to about 4 au and small substructures may be missed

evidence.quote: Given our resolution, which limits detection to structures as small as approximately 4 au
which points to a potential bias introduced by resolution where very small substructures may remain undetected in the smallest disks

limitations_admitted.value: Sz130 extended emission below 300 kilo-lambda could not be fit; flux 41% lower than literature

evidence.quote: In the case of Sz130, this resulted in a lower flux (41% lower) compared to the literature values.

limitations_admitted.value: Flux discrepancies may result from missing short baselines

evidence.quote: Some discrepancies could arise from the absence of short baselines in our observations, potentially leading to the loss of extended emission flux.

limitations_admitted.value: Planet masses for several disks exceed DBNets rejection threshold and should be interpreted with caution

evidence.quote: the planet masses for these disks should be interpreted with caution

referee_caveats_inferred: Most disks are fitted with a single Gaussian even when marginally resolved; radii of unresolved disks rely on fixed face-on geometry and are model dependent

Dust masses depend on fixed assumptions in the RADMC-3D grid (Sigma proportional to 1/r, DSHARP opacities, face-on, no stellar temperature dependence), so the optical depth conclusion is model dependent
Heterogeneous sample: images and parameters from many programmes with different resolution and processing; five disks lack very high resolution
Abstract planet separations 2 to 74 au disagree with Table 2 (up to 117 au for IM Lup) and the Discussion (14-117 au)
Planet masses from DBNets assume planet-carved gaps and cavity positions chosen from fitted ring parameters; many exceed the rejection threshold
No self-calibration, and flux scale uncertainty is not propagated into radii or masses

data_public_as_stated.value: Project codes and PIs listed; archival projects 2018.1.01458.S and 2017.1.00388.S described as archival data; public status of the Cycle 9 program not stated

evidence.quote: Additionally, we incorporated archival ALMA data to complete the sample of Lupus disks at high resolution (project code: 2018.1.01458.S, PI: Yen, Hsi-Wei).

missing_for_reproduction: Cleaning masks, thresholds, image sizes and uv-tapers for each image
MCMC priors, bounds and per-source walker/step counts for all 38 modelled sources
RADMC-3D setup details (scale height, flaring, photon counts) and the inversion procedure for the model grid
DBNets settings and the per-source gap or cavity radii used
Data for several comparison disks come from in-prep papers (Rota et al.; Bosschaart et al.)
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: About 40 pointed observations across 5 projects (10 EBs for the main Band 6 program); likely a few hundred GB of raw data, with continuum-only products much smaller
reproducibility.score_reason: Project codes, CASA version, tclean scales, weighting per source and model tables are given and results are numeric, but masks, priors, per-source MCMC settings, RT-grid details and DBNets configuration are missing, and no code is released
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Observations are ALMA archive projects with stated codes, imaging and visibility-fit recipes are largely specified, and main results (radii, SLR slope, dust masses) are numeric, though fine settings must be inferred
